summary.intent: Complete Phase 23 (Rust SDK Extraction) gap closure execution, then run a security review on the phase's cryptographic code and increase Rust test coverage to satisfy Codecov requirements for PR #352.
summary.outcome: Phase 23 fully completed with all 8 plans executed and bookkeeping committed. Security review identified and fixed 2 HIGH findings (Ed25519 zeroization). 163 new unit tests added across 3 Rust crates (168 total). PR #352 created, merged with main, and CI failures fixed.

repo: Phase 23 is 'rust-sdk-extraction' — extracts crypto, core, fuse, sdk, and api crates from the desktop app monolith into a workspace of 5 independent crates.
The workspace uses a vendored fuser crate at apps/desktop/src-tauri/vendor/fuser patched via [patch.crates-io] in the root Cargo.toml — this applies workspace-wide including on Windows builds.
Ed25519 private key material in generate_ed25519_keypair was returned as bare Vec<u8>, leaving key bytes in freed memory; callers were wrapping with Zeroizing::new() redundantly.
ed25519-dalek's SigningKey only zeroes on drop when the 'zeroize' feature flag is explicitly enabled in the dependency declaration.
fetch_and_populate_folder and resolve_file_pointers_blocking existed as dead code in both platform paths (macOS/Linux operations.rs and Windows operations.rs) with no external callers.
CI runs cargo llvm-cov --workspace on Linux for Rust coverage reporting to Codecov; tests added to any workspace crate are automatically included.
The cross-language parity CI job was missing pnpm version specification (needs version: 10 to match other jobs); other jobs in ci.yml correctly specify version: 10.
KeyState and CipherBoxFS key fields already use Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> with proper clear() on logout/unmount — the zeroization pattern is established but was not applied to keypair generation output.

code.finding: generate_ed25519_keypair return type changed from (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) to (Vec<u8>, Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>) to wrap private key material; callers in write_ops.rs were wrapping redundantly with Zeroizing::new()

After return type change, ipns_private_key.try_into() for Vec<u8>->[u8;32] conversion needed to use Vec::from(ipns_private_key).try_into() since Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> doesn't implement TryInto<[u8;32]> directly
Same try_into() pattern on Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> required Vec::from() unwrap before conversion
fetch_and_populate_folder and resolve_file_pointers_blocking were dead code — resolve_* only called from fetch_*, and fetch_* had no external callers; ~181 lines removed across both platform files
Build script called unimplemented!() on non-Linux without libfuse feature, causing Windows CI failures. Fixed by adding cfg(target_os = "windows") early return.
Cross-language vector parity job missing 'version: 10' on pnpm/action-setup@v4 step, causing CI failure
ed25519-dalek workspace dependency needed features = ["zeroize"] added for SigningKey to zero on drop

workflow: When a GSD executor agent disconnects mid-plan, spot-checking git log for phase-plan commit patterns and verifying acceptance criteria manually is the correct recovery path before creating SUMMARY.md.
1Password SSH signing agent can be flaky on first commit attempt; retrying 2-3 times before concluding it's unavailable is appropriate.
Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> auto-derefs to &[u8] transparently but does NOT implement TryInto<[u8;32]> — must use Vec::from(zeroizing_val).try_into() for array conversions.
Parallel agent spawning for independent test-writing tasks (one agent per crate) is effective; all three completed successfully and independently.
The security review command (security:review) produces a structured report at .planning/security/REVIEW-[timestamp].md and should be committed to the PR branch.

friction: 1Password SSH agent failed 3 consecutive commit attempts mid-session, requiring user to manually retry later after returning from AFK.
GSD executor agent connection refused (ConnectionRefused API error) mid-wave-1 execution, requiring manual resumption and spot-check recovery.
Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> TryInto incompatibility was a non-obvious consequence of the return type change — required checking multiple call sites across platform-specific files.
The vendored fuser build.rs failure on Windows was not caught locally (macOS dev environment) and only surfaced in CI.
gh CLI output for failed CI jobs required multiple bash command iterations to extract actual compiler errors from verbose download/upload noise.
open_items: AES-CTR lacks client-side CID integrity verification — client doesn't verify the IPFS CID after fetching bytes, leaving it vulnerable to bit-flip from a compromised relay (HIGH finding from security review, not fixed this session).

file_ipns_private_key in write_ops.rs (line ~174) uses ed25519_dalek directly with SigningKey::to_bytes().to_vec() rather than going through generate_ed25519_keypair — this secondary key generation path was noted as out of scope for the zeroization fix.
~30 test case suggestions from the security review (for AES-CTR attack scenarios, nonce reuse detection, replay attacks) were documented in the report but not implemented as actual tests.
Medium-priority security findings (4 MEDIUM, 5 LOW from review) were not addressed — only the 2 HIGH findings were fixed.
